Tr.Crl.P.No.83 of 2024
Order:

This Transfer Criminal Petition is filed by the petitioner to transfer STC.NI.No.363 of 2024 pending on the file of the learned I Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Khammam to the file of the learned III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad.

entities.text: I Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Khammam
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard Sri P. Vamsheedhar Reddy, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners as well as Parimala Parigi, learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.2.
3.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that respondent No.2, filed a private complaint against the petitioner and her husband, which was referred to the Police Station Borabanda.

He further submitted that the same respondent filed another complaint, STC NI No.363/2024, under the NI Act and IPC, despite having no transactions with respondent No.4 in Khammam, as all transactions took place in Hyderabad.
He further submitted that respondent No.2 has maliciously and vexatiously filed multiple cases, abusing the law and causing SKS,J undue hardship.
Transferring the case to Hyderabad would allow for judicious resolution of both cases, preventing irreparable loss to the petitioner.

Therefore, he prayed the Court to transfer STC.NI.No.363 of 2024 pending on the file of the learned I Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Khammam to the file of the learned III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad.

entities.text: I Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Khammam
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 submitted that the jurisdiction for filing cases under the NI Act lies in Khammam, whereas the jurisdiction for filing complaints under Sections 406 and 420 of the IPC lies in Hyderabad.
He argued that the cases are being tried in their respective jurisdictional Courts.
Therefore, he prayed that the Court dismiss the transfer criminal petition.

5. Considering the submissions of both parties and the material on record, it appears that the transactions in question stem from the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) signed by the petitioner and respondent No.2.
The non-performance of this MOU led to the registration of criminal cases and the issuance of a cheque based on the terms and conditions of the MOU.

Therefore, the Court deems it fit to transfer STC.NI.No.363 of 2024 from the file of the learned I Additional SKS,J Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Khammam, to the file of the learned III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Khammam
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 6. Accordingly, the Transfer Criminal Petition is allowed.
